_comment: NickelOS: disk_layout_v2 with ChromeOS Flex's partition sizes. KERN-A/B 64 MiB and EFI-SYSTEM 256 MiB (v2 default 32/64) leave room for bigger kernels and for crdyshim + crdyboot + the GRUB fallback in the ESP. Installed devices' ROOT-A/B partitions are 6 GiB (Dresden, 2026-10-18; v2: 4 GiB): NickelOS's root holds the OS with Gentoo's packages and Portage (docs/unified.md), and partition sizes can't change on installed devices, so the room is set before the first release. The root filesystem is 4800 MiB with one inode per 32 KiB (v2: 2300 MiB, one per 64 KiB; 4000 MiB until 2026-10-19, when Gentoo's Mesa and LLVM 22 came in for Chrome and Linux apps, vision decision 5); it grows inside the 6 GiB partitions with no repartitioning. The images' own ROOT partitions (usb, recovery) are 5 GiB, enough for the filesystem and its verity hashes. The factory installer keeps its own (460 MiB), which the common size would override.
